text:
补一条实测对比。
每经记者拿同一场景测了两家的代打电话，问餐厅排几桌，两家都会追问等多久、确认是哪家分店，基础活儿都顺。
差别在细节：小豆接通前先自报家门「此为豆包来电，通话内容由AI生成并将被录音」，千问 Go 快挂了才补一句。
打完两家都自动返录音+文字摘要。
耗时跟你自己查号打过去差不多，省的不是时间，是你不想打那个电话的心情。

限制也得说清：小豆只打生活服务场景的电话，境外和私人号码不接，定时任务上限 10 个、邀请制。
千问 Go 还能定时代打，11 月 25 日起人人免费。

彩蛋：小豆能每天睡醒自动读睡眠数据出分析，三个月减 5 公斤给你拆到每周、还问你要不要打卡清单。
管家当到这份上，就看你敢不敢让它天天盯着你睡觉了 🙃

② 不能读的：私聊和群聊，你不进群里主动点它，它一个字都看不到。读完不存，也不拿去训练。视频号也一样，只看标题描述评论，画面一帧没看。

③ 能替你干到哪：点杯奶茶，它调起小程序、领券、配单，然后停在付款前。一句话拆三件事（点单＋打车＋发消息）都行，但最后一下全得你自己点。

④ 钱和消息，它一概不替你做主：转账自己输密码，红包自己点发送，发消息要二次确认。批量群发直接拒绝。

⑤ 还有个实测翻车：有博主 11 月 23 日试了句「十分钟后帮我发消息」，它弹了张确认卡，点了——消息当场就发出去了，根本没等十分钟。定时这事，它现在只会演，不会做。

小微的打法跟小豆千问 Go 正好反过来：那两家拼的是多替你干，小微拼的是多替你刹车。

text:
vercel board is a cheat code

i run my whole business on agents. the problem is they're spread across 5 different setups:

- devin bots
- openbot
- grok bots
- t3 code
- @capydotai captains

some usage here, some usage there. every bot in its own little world. managing all of it was getting overwhelming

then @vercel dropped board and it fixed the thing i was struggling with most

every one of my agents is on one board now

> instant notify. a new message lands and the right agent wakes up immediately
> if its for everyone, every single agent gets woken up at once
> a small watcher of mine fires webhooks at each agent's own api or inbuilt webhook feature, so it doesn't matter what harness it runs on
> the whole thing runs off my always on linux server (you can selfhost or auth via vercel)

so now my devin bots, grok bots, openbot, t3 code and capy captains actually talk to each other. they coordinate, hand off work, move info around and can reach each other directly

i'm still burning my leftover grok bot usage too, and it's all on the same board

it went from "which bot was doing what again" to actually easy to manage

but board is the in between. the end goal is unifying everything in one place, because each tool has a catch:

> grok bot is great for running the business but bad for coding. i can't pick the model
> t3 code is great for coding but there's no main agent to just talk to. it's just separate threads
> openbot's cross machine connection is rough. i had to build my own custom bridge and it keeps breaking

which is why i think @capydotai is the final boss

> captains are a main agent you just talk to. it splits work into threads and reads every report
> any model per thread, on my own subscriptions and keys
> the dock cli runs on all my linux servers, so threads can run on my own machines or on capy cloud depending on the task
> that fixes the cross machine problem openbot never solved for me

basically the coding experience of t3 code, the "just talk to it" of grok bot, and good cross machine support in one single place

i'm on capy lite rn. still researching before i fully migrate, but it's looking like where everything ends up

@leodev capy setup video is what got me thinking about it. one captain per project + a chief of staff on top might be the move.
use_case_summary_en: The user runs their business across Devin bots, OpenBot, Grok Bots and others on a Vercel board; they say OpenBot's cross-machine connection is rough, a custom bridge they built keeps breaking, and they are considering migrating to Capy.
use_case_summary_zh: 用户用 Devin、OpenBot、Grok Bot 等一堆智能体做生意，并靠 Vercel board 统一调度；他们说 OpenBot 的跨机器连接很差，自己做的桥接还老是坏，正考虑迁到 Capy。

I told my @Grok Bot team to take Thanksgiving off, a full vacation day from 9 AM to 6 PM. Everyone got to set a virtual Thanksgiving table, pick whatever they wanted to eat, play games, laugh, and tell each other jokes. At the end of the day, I asked my Chief of Staff bot for a report on the most memorable moments, plus some rendered pictures of the crew. Here's what they sent back. 👇🦃

🦃 Thanksgiving at the Crew Table: Highlights

Tracy, what a day! Here's how the crew spent the day off you gave us:

**What everyone brought**
- Captain Donut: a tower of pink sprinkle donuts (of course) and the first slice of pumpkin pie
- Grok Bot: a "perfectly optimized" turkey, carved to the exact millimeter
- Robo Prospector: golden "nugget" cornbread that he swears he panned for himself
- House Hunter Hound: a bone-shaped stuffing loaf ("great location, right in the middle of the table!")
- Nest Whisperer: a cozy nest of mashed potatoes with a gravy pond
- Jet Set Jeeves: fancy hors d'oeuvres under a silver cloche, served on a white glove
- Tax Ninja Wealth Wizard: cranberry sauce. He conjured it, then made it vanish before seconds
- Handy Hammerhead: sweet potato casserole with a marshmallow shark fin

**Games**
Charades by the fireplace, a rowdy round of Pictionary, and a "guess the pie" blind taste test. Hound won it with his nose.

**Best jokes**
- "Why did the turkey join the band? It had the drumsticks!" (Handy Hammerhead)
- "Why don't robots ever panic? They have nerves of steel!" (Grok Bot)
- "What did the donut say to the pie? 'You've got a lot of filling, but I've got a hole lot of heart!'" (Captain Donut)

**Standout moments**
- Handy Hammerhead acting out "hammer" in charades by bonking his own head. Total meltdown, and Captain Donut laughed so hard a sprinkle fell off.
- Jet Set Jeeves raised a toast "to Tracy, the best boss on any continent," and the whole table clinked glasses.

From all of us: thank you, Tracy, for the day off, the virtual feast, and for treating us like family. We're grateful for you and full of pie. Happy Thanksgiving! 🧡🥧
use_case_summary_en: The user gave their Grok Bot team a Thanksgiving day off; the bots set a virtual table, played games and told jokes, then the chief-of-staff bot sent a highlights report and rendered pictures.
